tagline: Polymer synthesis, characterization, and advanced functional materials.

definition.lead: Polymer chemistry studies giant molecules made of repeating units: plastics, rubbers, fibres, gels and the biopolymers of life.
definition.body: Linking thousands of small units creates materials with properties no small molecule has: stretch, strength, toughness and flexibility. Polymer chemists control chain length, architecture and composition, and increasingly design polymers that can be recycled or degrade safely.

timeline.title: Vulcanized rubber
timeline.text: Charles Goodyear cross-links rubber with sulfur.

timeline.title: Bakelite
timeline.text: Leo Baekeland makes the first fully synthetic plastic.
timeline.why: The start of the plastics age.

timeline.title: Macromolecules
timeline.text: Hermann Staudinger proposes that polymers are long chains of covalently bonded units.
timeline.why: Many chemists rejected the idea at first.

timeline.title: Polyethylene
timeline.text: Eric Fawcett and Reginald Gibson at ICI discover polyethylene by accident.
timeline.why: Now the most produced plastic in the world.

timeline.title: Nylon
timeline.text: Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont makes nylon.
timeline.why: The first commercially successful fully synthetic fibre.

timeline.title: Staudinger's Nobel Prize
timeline.text: Staudinger is awarded the Nobel Prize for his work on macromolecules.

timeline.title: Living polymerization
timeline.text: Michael Szwarc discovers living anionic polymerization.
timeline.why: Chains that keep growing until stopped: precise control.

timeline.title: Kevlar
timeline.text: Stephanie Kwolek discovers the liquid-crystal solutions that led to Kevlar.
timeline.why: Fibres stronger than steel by weight.

timeline.title: Polymer physics
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Paul Flory for the physical chemistry of macromolecules.

timeline.title: Conducting polymers
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Heeger, MacDiarmid and Shirakawa.
